claims.statement: Each Open-Inspect session id maps to exactly one SessionDO Durable Object instance via env.SESSION.idFromName(sessionId); the class is a thin Cloudflare adapter that forwards fetch, webSocketMessage, webSocketClose, webSocketError, and alarm to a platform-neutral SessionServer.

SessionDO.ensureInitialized applies the SQLite schema (initSchema) and then eagerly builds the whole collaborator graph via createSessionRuntime; the runtime is published only after construction succeeds, so a throw leaves the activation uninitialized and the next event retries initialization instead of dereferencing an undefined runtime.

SessionDO.alarm calls ensureInitialized(false) so alarm delivery does not re-arm the same wake-up; every other entry point initializes with rehydration of the persisted alarm deadline (runtime.alarms.rehydrate runs on a background task).

createSessionRuntime (session/components.ts) is the composition root for one session runtime: it builds every repository, service, and handler eagerly in topological tiers over the SessionPlatform {ctx, sql, db}, and returns only the narrow surface SessionDO needs — the log, the SessionServer, alarm rehydration, and an internals record reserved for integration tests.

The composition root eagerly constructs both provider factories (createSandboxProviderFromEnv and createSourceControlProviderFromEnv); they throw on misconfigured deployments (missing provider credentials, invalid SCM_PROVIDER, GitLab without a token, Bitbucket), deliberately failing every session request at initialization before any session state is written.

The session-scoped logger injects session_id per emit through a latched public-session-id resolver: before /internal/init writes the row it resolves to the Durable Object id, and it upgrades to session_name || id the moment the row exists; children created for request correlation inherit the injection, and the latched resolver never captures the DO id fallback.

SessionHttpDispatcher routes by exact (method, path) string equality against the internal route table, routes WebSocket upgrade requests to the connection authenticator (never counted as a route metric), returns 404 for unmatched routes, and logs every matched request as do.request with method, path, status, duration_ms, handler_ms and outcome; failures are rethrown but still recorded as outcome error.

Internal request correlation is threaded through request-scoped logger children: the dispatcher creates a child carrying x-trace-id/x-request-id headers only when present (never mutating the session logger), and the router-side SessionRuntimeClient injects those headers into every DO fetch.

SessionInternalPaths constants in session/contracts.ts are imported by both the internal router (session/http/routes.ts) and the control-plane router's runtime client; no caller hardcodes an internal path, so the two sides cannot drift, and buildSessionInternalUrl composes them onto the synthetic http://internal origin.

The internal route table is exact-match transport wiring only: createSessionInternalRoutes maps each SessionInternalPath constant to one (GET or POST) method plus a handler closure wired in the composition root; routes.test.ts pins the full method/path set 1:1 against the constants.

ESLint enforces the session composition boundaries with no-restricted-imports: only durable-object.ts may import the composition root (components.ts), only the worker entrypoint (index.ts) may import the adapter, and only composition roots may read env.DB.

The SessionDO schema lives in session/schema.ts: initSchema runs SCHEMA_SQL (fresh-DO base tables), the numbered MIGRATIONS list (45 entries tracked in _schema_migrations), and INDEXES_SQL on every activation; shared table-SQL constants (SESSION_REPOSITORIES_TABLE_SQL, ATTACHMENTS_TABLE_SQL, SESSION_DIFF_TABLE_SQL, SESSION_ALARM_STATE_TABLE_SQL) are reused by migration 31 and later entries so the fresh-DO and migrated-DO paths cannot diverge.

The DO SQLite schema enforces session invariants in the engine: the partial unique index idx_messages_one_processing allows at most one message with status 'processing' per session, and idx_messages_client_request_id enforces web-prompt client_request_id uniqueness.

Repositories over SqlStorage use ctx.storage.transactionSync (injected per runtime as transaction) for multi-table atomicity; startMessageProcessing claims a pending message with a compare-and-set UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 WHERE status = 'processing') RETURNING id inside one transaction and inserts the canonical user_message timeline event in the same transaction.

The event repository assigns timeline_sequence as MAX + 1 inside the INSERT; token and execution_complete events upsert on deterministic ids (token:<messageId>, execution_complete:<messageId>) so streams are idempotent while each upsert keeps a fresh timeline position, and the unique timeline index (idx_events_timeline_sequence) is engine-enforced.

SessionEventStream serves three read paths: getReplay (latest 500 events excluding heartbeat for the subscribed snapshot), getHistoryPage (cursor-paged backwards slices, limit clamped 1-500), and listEvents (HTTP GET /internal/events with type/messageId/limit filters); malformed persisted events are skipped, not fatal.

SessionSnapshotReader.readSessionSnapshot runs inside ctx.storage.transactionSync so the subscribed snapshot (session row, sandbox row, artifacts, timeline replay, prompt queue, spawn error) is a consistent cut.

SessionWebSocketManagerImpl is the single owner of the Cloudflare WebSocket API: client sockets are accepted with a wsid:<id> tag and sandbox sockets with sandbox plus sid:<sandboxId> tags, and classify(ws) reads ctx.getTags so socket kinds are recognizable after hibernation without in-memory state.

Sandbox socket recovery in getSandboxSocket validates the persisted sandbox.modal_sandbox_id against the sid: tag, closes sockets whose identity changed, and refuses to re-adopt WebSockets when the sandbox row is terminal (stopped, failed, stale) because a zombie socket can report OPEN after hibernation while the DO slept mid-close-handshake.

Client WebSocket identity survives hibernation through the ws_client_mapping table: completeClientSubscription persists the wsid-to-participant mapping after the snapshot handoff, and getClientInfo rebuilds ClientInfo from that row after hibernation, closing the socket with 4002 when no mapping exists.

Every client socket must subscribe within WS_AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000 or it is closed with code 4008; sockets that are synchronizing, hold in-memory ClientInfo, or have a persisted ws_client_mapping row are exempt, which is what lets hibernation-recovered connections survive the timeout.

Hibernation-level keepalive is wired in the composition root: ctx.setWebSocketAutoResponse pairs JSON-stringified {"type":"ping"} with {"type":"pong", timestamp} so the runtime answers pings without waking the Durable Object.

WebSocket admission orders checks deliberately: sandbox upgrades validate the sandbox id and bearer token first, then re-read the session status after the non-storage token-hash await (so a concurrent cancel/archive is honored), rejecting terminal sessions and reconnect-blocked sandbox statuses with 410; a successful sandbox connect resets the spawning flag, marks the sandbox ready, broadcasts sandbox_status, schedules the inactivity check, and kicks processMessageQueue in the background.

Client subscription authenticates the ws token hash against participants.ws_auth_token with a 24-hour TTL (close 4001 for missing/invalid/expired) and completes the snapshot-to-stream handoff in a non-async method — read snapshot, send subscribed, register client, persist ws mapping — so no event can interleave between the final read and registration.

SessionMessageRouter validates sandbox frames against sandboxEventSchema and client frames against clientMessageSchema; binary frames are ignored; before authentication only ping and subscribe are valid; fetch_history is rate-limited to one page per 200 ms per connection; and the default switch arm uses 'satisfies never' so adding a ClientMessage variant without an explicit handler is a compile error.

SessionSandboxEventProcessor builds one per-event context (one clock reading, message attribution preferring the event's own messageId over the current processing message) and dispatches to family handlers; the five critical event types (execution_complete, error, snapshot_ready, push_complete, push_error) get an ack to the sandbox only after their handler finishes, and family handlers never see ackId.

SessionDisconnectHandler applies close policy by classification: sandbox closes schedule a reconnect check through the lifecycle manager unless a newer sandbox socket already replaced this one or the sandbox status blocks reconnection; client closes broadcast presence_leave only when no other socket of that participant remains; the peer close is always reciprocated.

SessionMessageQueue is the session execution engine: prompt admission runs idempotency lookup, capacity check, and insert in one synchronous turn; client_request_id dedup compares author plus a request fingerprint (hash of participant, content, model, reasoning effort, attachment ids) and raises PROMPT_REQUEST_CONFLICT for a reused id with different content; MAX_UNFINISHED_PROMPTS caps pending plus processing counts.

processMessageQueue defers dispatch when no sandbox socket exists: the message stays pending and the sandbox spawns on a background task (a snapshot restore can take tens of seconds and awaiting it would hold the prompt HTTP response past bot request timeouts); the persisted pending message dispatches when the sandbox WebSocket connects and the upgrade path re-runs processMessageQueue.

Prompt dispatch claims the message via startMessageProcessing (CAS inside a transaction), records the user_message event, sends the SandboxCommand with the resolved model, reasoning effort, and author git identity, then arms the execution-timeout deadline through the alarm scheduler; a failed send reverts the claim (updateMessageToPending deletes the user_message event), terminates the unresponsive sandbox, and resumes the queue.

Stop semantics: stopExecution marks the processing message failed, upserts a synthetic execution_complete broadcast so clients flush buffered tokens, sets stop_confirmation_deadline = now + STOP_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS (15 s) and arms it, then forwards {type:stop} to the sandbox; a sandbox that does not confirm within the deadline is terminated and the queue resumes.

failStuckProcessingMessage only marks the processing message failed and broadcasts — it deliberately does not send a stop to the sandbox or re-dispatch, avoiding races where a new prompt reaches a sandbox being shut down.

SessionStatusService.transition fans every status change to three projections: connected clients (session_status broadcast), the D1 session index (updateStatus with a monotonic updated_at + 1 guard, child-admission finalization on active, and terminal metrics for settled statuses), and the parent session's DO via a backgrounded POST /internal/child-session-update; reconcileAfterExecution settles status from queue depth plus terminal-message outcome, and an empty session deliberately falls back to created so the abandoned-draft sweep can reclaim it.

All session deadlines share the Durable Object's single alarm slot through createEarliestAlarmScheduler: the PersistedAlarmDeadlineStore singleton row (session_alarm_state, authoritative pending_deadline plus in_flight_deadline) is updated before the runtime ctx.storage alarm, mutations are serialized through one promise chain, schedule keeps the earliest deadline, cancel clears both stores, rehydrate reasserts after a cold start, and rearmPending reasserts after an in-flight delivery.

handleAlarmDelivery tracks the delivered deadline separately so retries cannot acknowledge a replacement: beginDelivery records in_flight_deadline (short-circuiting when cancelled), the handler runs, rearmPending reasserts only when the delivery was real, then completeDelivery clears in_flight.

The alarm handler (createAlarmHandler) orders three responsibilities: recover an expired stop confirmation, enforce the execution timeout by failing a message stuck in processing past getExecutionTimeoutMs (reasserting that message's deadline when not yet timed out, because an earlier lifecycle alarm may have consumed the slot), then delegate to lifecycleManager.handleAlarm — non-no_action outcomes also fail a stuck processing message as defense-in-depth, and sandbox_terminated resumes the queue.

SessionServer is platform-neutral over generic Connection and Client types (unit-tested with plain strings in server.test.ts): the DO adapter is the only production caller, and hibernation-restored callbacks reconstruct the runtime on first touch before any server entry point is reachable.

The control-plane Worker forwards WebSocket upgrades at /sessions/:id/ws: it validates the session exists in the D1 SessionIndexStore, resolves SESSION.idFromName, forwards the upgrade request to the DO, and returns the 101 with the DO's socket plus Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

Session creation is a D1-first two-step flow: the D1 SessionIndexStore row (status 'created') is written before the DO is asked to POST /internal/init, and the public session id is derived as session_name || id at read time — which is why the latched logger resolver and status projections all use resolvePublicSessionId; initialize.test.ts pins the ordering and DO-failure compensation.
